items.h: Two big plays against New Orleans
items.s: Thomas brought in two of three targets for 56 yards and added a 30-yard carry during the Bears' 21-13 win over the Saints on Sunday. Thomas was cleared to play Sunday after working through an ankle issue that prevented him from practicing Friday. The ankle didn't appear to bother him, as he turned his first touch of the game into a 30-yard rush midway through the second quarter before connecting with Caleb Williams on passes for 40 and 16 yards in the third and fourth, respectively. It was the rookie third-round wideout's best performance of the season, and while Chicago boasts talented pass catchers like Luther Burden, Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland, Thomas' big-play potential could be…

items.h: Zavion Thomas sees three touches in Week 11
items.s: Zavion Thomas caught two of his three targets for 56 yards while also rushing oncer for 30 yards in the Bears' 21-13 win over the Saints in Week 11. Thomas flashed explosive speed in The Chicago offense Sunday, averaging 28.7 yards per touch in the win. The wideout remains difficult to trust despite his explosive play potential entering a Week 12 contest against the Detroit Lions.

Thomas (ankle) is active for Sunday's matchup against New Orleans. Thomas popped up on the practice report as a nonparticipant Friday due to an ankle issue and was initially deemed questionable for Sunday. However, the rookie will ultimately be able to play through the issue. Thomas typically has a minimal role on offense, as he's caught more than one pass in only one of his nine appearances so far. However, he's worked as Chicago's primary kickoff returner and should again contribute in that role against the Saints.

Thomas (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's matchup against the Saints. Thomas appears to have picked up an injury in the Bears' lead-up to Week 11, as he did not participate in Friday's practice. The rookie third-rounder acts as the team's top kick-return option. Should he not play, Josh Blackwell may take over duties on special teams.

Thomas hauled in one of his two targets for 13 yards and returned three kicks for 88 yards during Chicago's win versus Tampa Bay on Sunday. Thomas continues to see limited action offensively, playing just five snaps Sunday and no more than 15 on offense in any game this season, though he did manage to record his seventh reception of the season. The rookie third-round pick should continue to see the majority of his action come on special teams, and he's now amassed 715 kick-return yards across nine outings this season.

items.h: Zavion Thomas sees three targets in Week 6
items.s: Zavion Thomas caught all three of his targets for 25 yards in the Bears' 31-23 win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 6. Thomas has been a non-factor in the Chicago offense to this point, finishing with less than 30 receiving yards in each of the first six contests. The pass-catcher remains best left out of lineups in all formats ahead of a Week 7 contest against the New England Patriots.

items.h: Zavion Thomas sees two touches in Week 5
items.s: Zavion Thomas caught his only target for 11 yards while also rushing once for 11 yards in the Bears' 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 5. Thomas has been non-existent in the Chicago offense to begin the season, seeing one target or less in each of the first five contests. The wideout can be left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 6 contest against the Atlanta Falcons.

items.h: Zavion Thomas' Preseason Hype is Fizzling Out
items.s: Chicago Bears wide receiver Zavion Thomas drew plenty of hype heading into the 2026 season, but he has quickly found himself trending back downward. The rookie demonstrated speed and versatility in college, and he caught five passes for 140 yards and one touchdown in the NFL preseason. However, Week 1 came around and he didn't play a single offensive snap. Despite his impressive summer, Thomas is clearly buried on the depth chart behind Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III, Kalif Raymond, and Jahdae Walker. He's still worth stashing in dynasty fantasy football, especially because his rookie status makes him eligible for the taxi squad in most leagues. However, he can be avoided entirely in…

items.h: Zavion Thomas an Intriguing Deep-League Stash Candidate Entering 2026
items.s: Entering 2026, Chicago Bears rookie wide receiver Zavion Thomas projects to be his team's WR4 behind Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III (groin), and Kalif Raymond. Bears tight end Colston Loveland is also expected to be heavily featured in the team's passing game, pushing Thomas even further down the target pecking order. However, Thomas showed an ability to impact games as both a pass-catcher and a rusher during his college career, recording 488 receiving yards, 99 rushing yards, and five total touchdowns across 13 games at LSU in 2025. items.h: Zavion Thomas Sets the Tone by Going 97 Yards on His First NFL Play
items.s: Chicago Bears rookie wide receiver Zavion Thomas did not participate in the team's first two preseason outings as he dealt with minor knee soreness earlier in camp, but he wasted no time making his presence felt on Saturday night. Thomas got behind the defense with a double move on the first play of his NFL career and outraced everyone for a 97-yard touchdown to set the tone in a 24-15 win over the Titans. He would finish the night with five catches on five targets and a team-leading 140 yards to go with his game-opening score, showcasing his value as a potential third or fourth receiver in what projects to be a high-powered Chicago offense. The Bears have no lack of playmakers atop the…

items.h: Shows off speed on long TD
items.s: Thomas secured all five targets for 140 yards and a touchdown, ran back one kickoff for 22 yards and returned one punt for 39 yards in the Bears' 24-15 preseason win over the Titans on Saturday. Making his preseason debut, the lightning-fast rookie third-round pick wasted no time showing off his elite speed, hauling in a Tyson Bagent pass at the Bears' 33-yard line and motoring down the right side of the field for a 97-yard touchdown. Thomas also was impressive on both of his returns, and he comfortably led Chicago in receiving yards on the night.
